rfi.title: Denmark welcomes deal with US over Greenland after Trump annexation threats

rfi.title: Europe weighs the cost of sending its own astronauts into space
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron wants Europe to develop its own way of sending astronauts into space within a decade. Europe already builds rockets and satellites and sends astronauts to the International Space Station – but it still relies on American spacecraft to get them there. As the global space sector expands, the question is whether Europe should invest in closing that gap, and what it would take to do so.

rfi.title: France calls on Moscow to reverse takeover of European assets
rfi.description: France has called on Moscow to "reverse" its decision to take control of assets belonging to European companies still operating in Russia, including Swiss food giant Nestle and three French groups. The Kremlin defends the takeover as a justified measure against firms representing "unfriendly countries" that back Ukraine.

rfi.title: As far right gains ground in Germany, Berlin election tests Europe's centre
rfi.description: Berliners go to the polls on Sunday to elect the city-state’s parliament and district councils, in a vote taking place just two weeks after the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) secured a historic victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. The implications could extend beyond Germany.

rfi.title: Tiny French outpost off Canada the unlikely stage for new transatlantic courtship
rfi.description: A tiny piece of France just off Canada’s Atlantic coast will become the setting for a much bigger geopolitical story on Sunday, when President Emmanuel Macron welcomes Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to Saint-Pierre and Miquelon. The meeting brings Canada’s push for closer ties with Europe to a territory that has long sat at the crossroads of French, Canadian and US interests in the North Atlantic.

rfi.title: Russians vote for new parliament after campaign marked by near silence
rfi.description: Russians began voting on Friday in three days of parliamentary elections to choose the 450 members of the State Duma, after a campaign with little public debate or television coverage. rfi.title: Locked in Arctic ice, the floating lab studying climate and wildlife
rfi.description: A floating laboratory has begun drifting through Arctic sea ice on a mission set to last until late 2027, carrying scientists into one of the most isolated places on Earth. Built in France, the Tara Polar Station is carrying a crew of 12 to study biodiversity and the effects of climate change, as well as a dog to alert them to polar bears – and no one knows exactly where the ice will take them.

rfi.title: A city at the crossroads of history: Unearthing Gaza's ancient heritage

rfi.title: From Peru to the Philippines, defending the land comes at a deadly cost
rfi.description: People defending their land, forests and communities continue to face killings, arrests and intimidation around the world – with Latin America by far the most dangerous region, the environmental campaign group Global Witness has found. In the Philippines, one community resisting a mining project has told RFI of arrests, injuries and legal action against residents trying to stop work on their land.

rfi.title: Dry rivers and shrinking glaciers deepen global freshwater decline
rfi.description: Rivers around the world are running unusually dry as freshwater reserves continue to decline, leaving less water stored away to help countries through drought, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned. Glaciers and groundwater are also shrinking, while in Switzerland the retreat of Alpine ice is already forcing changes to infrastructure that supplies hydroelectric power.

rfi.title: French fishermen renew protest as France boosts aid over soaring fuel prices
rfi.description: French fishermen renewed protests over rising fuel costs on Thursday despite the government increasing subsidies for the sector and extending support for farmers and construction companies. Diesel prices are nearing a record high, fuelling wider concern over the cost of living and calls for protests reminiscent of the Yellow Vest movement, seven months before the presidential election.

Alors que Netflix devient le premier financeur de la création audiovisuelle et cinématographique, ils appellent les responsables politiques à se pencher sur le modèle de l’exception culturelle française.

france24fr.title: Arabie saoudite : des flammes visibles près de l'aéroport de Riyad après de fortes explosions
france24fr.description: Les habitants de la capitale saoudienne ont été réveillés dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche par une alerte de risque d'attaque suivie de deux fortes explosions. Une première à Riyad depuis la reprise des affrontements avec les Houthis du Yémen. "On a vu de la fumée noire et des flammes vers l'aéroport", a rapporté un habitant. L'AFP a constaté qu'un réservoir de carburant du géant pétrolier saoudien Aramco situé près de l'aéroport est en feu

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026, le récap’ : les démocrates croient en la victoire, l'IA s’invite dans la campagne
france24fr.description: La dernière ligne droite de la campagne pour les Midterms a commencé ! Stratégie, candidats, sondages… Chaque semaine, France 24 fait le point sur ce qu'il faut retenir. Un sondage du New York Times publié mardi est venu conforter les espoirs des démocrates de remporter en novembre non seulement la Chambre des représentants mais aussi le Sénat. Et sur le terrain, les candidats s'emparent du thème brûlant de l'IA, notamment via la question des data centers.

france24fr.title: Michel Marx : "Dans mon enfance, tout dans l'organisation du quotidien était lié à la Shoah"
france24fr.description: Chaque semaine, Judith Grimaldi reçoit un invité dans son podcast "Avec Judith". L'invité de ce samedi est Michel Marx, scénariste et écrivain. Une partie de sa famille a péri dans la Shoah. Un héritage lourd qui a marqué son enfance : ses parents ne rentraient pas dans les détails, mais ce drame les suivait partout. Depuis des années, il tente de reconstituer le puzzle. Sa quête l'a mené à échanger avec Simone Veil et Ginette Kolinka, dont l'histoire est liée à celle de ses proches disparus.

france24fr.title: Cuba : nouvelle panne de courant massive, la septième de l'année
france24fr.description: Cuba subit vendredi 18 septembre une nouvelle panne de courant généralisée, la septième depuis le début de l'année sur fond de grave pénurie de carburant dans l'île communiste, sous pression de Washington.

france24fr.title: Lady Diana : sa célèbre "Revenge Dress" bientôt aux enchères
france24fr.description: La célèbre robe noire portée par Lady Diana en 1994 entame une tournée internationale avant sa mise aux enchères à New York, le 9 décembre. La "Revenge Dress" sera exposée à Londres, Hong Kong, et Genève.

france24fr.title: Trump annonce le remboursement de la fête de mariage de son fils à un oligarque russe
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré, vendredi, que son fils Donald Trump Jr. rembourserait Umar Kremlev, un riche homme d’affaires russe ayant pris en charge des frais de festivités pour son mariage aux Bahamas en mai. Ces dépenses ont soulevé des interrogations sur le risque d'influence étrangère autour de la famille présidentielle.

france24fr.title: CAN 2027 - Sénégal : Patrick Vieira annonce sa première liste
france24fr.description: Pour ses débuts à la tête des Lions de la Teranga, Patrick Vieira a convoqué 29 joueurs pour les prochaines rencontres des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Sadio Mané, forfait en raison d’un problème physique, est absent de cette première sélection, qui comprend notamment le défenseur Malang Sarr, nouvel appelé.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : le pic d'Ebola n'a pas encore été atteint, selon Africa CDC
france24fr.description:
En République démocratique du Congo, le pic de l’épidémie d’Ebola n’est toujours pas confirmé, selon Africa CDC, l’agence sanitaire de l’Union africaine. Une position qui contraste avec celle des autorités congolaises, qui affirment depuis la semaine dernière que le pic a été atteint à la mi-août. Depuis son apparition en mai, l’épidémie a fait plus de 3 500 morts et enregistré plus de 7 400 cas confirmés en RD Congo, selon les dernières données disponibles.

france24fr.title: France : les trésors du patrimoine ouvrent leurs portes
france24fr.description: À l’occasion des Journées européennes du patrimoine, les 19 et 20 septembre 2026, des milliers de sites ouvrent exceptionnellement leurs portes au public partout en France. Cette 43e édition met notamment à l’honneur le patrimoine de la photographie et les sites en péril.

france24fr.title: Allemagne : Merz joue son avenir aux élections régionales de dimanche
france24fr.description: Le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz survivra-t-il aux scrutins régionaux de dimanche ? Le débat est ouvert après le récent échec électoral de son parti conservateur en Saxe-Anhalt où l'extrême droite a obtenu une écrasante victoire.

france24fr.title: Prix du carburant en France : l’aide aux gros rouleurs prolongée
france24fr.description: Le dispositif destiné aux gros rouleurs devait prendre fin à la fin du mois, mais le ministre du Commerce, Serge Papin, assure qu’il sera prolongé.

france24fr.title: L'Arabie saoudite assure que la Mecque a été attaquée, les Houthis protestent
france24fr.description:
Au moins 112 000 personnes ont été déplacées au Yémen et près de 3 000 autres se sont réfugiées à Djibouti, depuis la reprise des combats début septembre entre rebelles pro-iraniens Houthis et forces pro-gouvernementales, a rapporté vendredi l'ONU.Les Houthis sont parvenus la semaine dernière à prendre le contrôle du littoral de la mer Rouge, renforçant leur emprise sur le stratégique détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, qui relie l'Europe à l'Asie, via cette mer et le canal de Suez.

france24fr.title: Trump veut empêcher CNN et d'autres médias de venir à la Maison Blanche
france24fr.description: Donald Trump, intensifiant de manière spectaculaire sa guerre contre les médias, a annoncé vendredi interdire l'accès à la Maison Blanche aux chaînes de télévision CNN et MSNOW (anciennement MSNBC) ainsi qu'au média en ligne Politico "avec effet immédiat".

france24fr.title: L'Allemagne réduit les taxes sur le carburant avant un dimanche électoral crucial
france24fr.description: Berlin a annoncé, vendredi, des mesures d'allègements du prix du carburant, quelques jours après que le chancelier Friedrich Merz s'est engagé a faire un geste pour les consommateurs touchés par la flambée des prix. Ces mesures ont été annoncées avant deux scrutins régionaux à haut risque pour le pouvoir, fragilisé par une récente victoire du parti d'extrême droite AfD.

france24fr.title: Trump annonce avoir obtenu un "contrôle permanent" sur la sécurité du Groenland
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi 18 septembre avoir obtenu du Danemark et du Groenland un "contrôle permanent" de la sécurité du territoire arctique stratégique qui permettra, selon Washington, d'empêcher les adversaires des Etats-Unis, Chine et Russie en tête, de s'y installer.

france24fr.title: Ligue Europa : l’OM sombre à Besiktas
france24fr.description: Marseille s’est lourdement incliné en Turquie face à Besiktas (4-1) pour ses débuts en Ligue Europa. L’OM concède une quatrième défaite consécutive alors qu'il doit désormais préparer le Classique face au PSG, ce dimanche au Vélodrome.

france24fr.title: Équipe de France : Zinédine Zidane, le vent de fraîcheur chez les Bleus
france24fr.description: Pour sa première annonce de liste des Bleus vendredi, le nouveau sélectionneur a affirmé son choix de rupture avec Didier Deschamps. Cinq nouveaux joueurs, une philosophie de jeu portée vers l'avant... Avant ses débuts sur le banc en Ligue des Nations, "ZZ" fait souffler un vent de fraîcheur en Bleus.

france24fr.title: Une nouvelle espèce de chat sauvage découverte en Bolivie, une première en un siècle
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle espèce de félin sauvage a été découverte en Bolivie, une première dans le monde depuis plus d'un siècle, a annoncé à l'AFP une des scientifiques boliviennes ayant participé à cette découverte.

zeit.description: Die Bremer SPD setzt auf den erfahrenen Regierungschef als Spitzenkandidat. Mit leidenschaftlichem Wahlkampf wolle er seine dritte Amtszeit sichern, sagte Bovenschulte.

zeit.description: Naomi Beckwith ist die neue Leiterin der Documenta. Hier erzählt sie erstmals, wie sie nach den Skandalen um die Ausstellung weitermachen will.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Berichte von Cyberangriff  bei Wahlen in Russland +++ Trump unterzeichnet Sanktionspaket gegen Russland
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Grönland, Dänemark und die USA einigen sich: Das ist über die Zukunft der grössten Insel der Welt bekannt
nzz.description: Die Monate andauernden Verhandlungen über die Sicherheit von Grönland scheinen beendet. Donald Trump triumphiert, doch auch in Nuuk und Kopenhagen herrscht Erleichterung.

nzz.title: Trump ist bei Grönland einem Ziel näher gekommen, das die USA seit über hundert Jahren anstreben
nzz.description: Im Streit um die Arktisinsel haben die USA, Grönland und Dänemark einen Durchbruch verkündet. Obwohl der genaue Inhalt noch nicht bekannt ist, schreibt Trump dem Deal bereits eine historische Dimension zu.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Australien: Dort wo die Geopolitik an die Tür klopft.
nzz.description: Australien ist bekannt für seine flauschigen oder giftigen Tiere. Neben der netten Tiergeschichten berichtet Barbara Barkhausen als NZZ-Korrespondentin Asien-Pazifik auch über geopolitische Themen. In der neuesten Folge «NZZ Akzent» spricht sie mit Podcast-Host Simon Schaffer über die strategische Lage Australiens, dessen politischen Umbrüche und Veränderungen im Land.

nzz.title: Rolex mit Mondphase, Hublot mit Jeff Koons: Der Uhrenherbst bringt einige Überraschungen
nzz.description: Rolex belebt eine Uhr wieder, die italienische Sammler einst «grosse Bratpfanne» tauften. Hublot holt einen der bekanntesten Pop-Art-Künstler ans Handgelenk, und Blancpain setzt mit einer winzigen mechanischen Uhr ein unerwartetes Zeichen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Trump entlarvt die Show von Big Tech – auch Bern und Berlin sollten sich nicht blenden lassen
nzz.description: Die Weltuntergangsszenarien des Silicon Valley sind Kalkül. Politik und Wirtschaft tun gut daran, der Inszenierung von Big Tech mit eigener Datensouveränität statt Angst zu begegnen.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK MIT DATEN - Der deutsche Exodus in die Schweiz
nzz.description: Deutsche Auswanderer zieht es vor allem ins helvetische Nachbarland. Die Gründe dafür sind eindeutig.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Europäische Zentralbank: vier Präsidenten, drei Schritte in die falsche Richtung
nzz.description: Die EZB hat sich in den vergangenen zwei Jahrzehnten vom «market maker of last resort» über den «lender of last resort» für marode Staaten zum «Mädchen für alles» entwickelt. Das hat der Institution geschadet.

nzz.title: Reicht es Ende Monat nicht mehr für die Miete, bitten immer mehr Menschen online um Geld. Die Plattform Gofundme verdient damit
nzz.description: Medizinische Versorgung, gestiegene Heizkosten: Die Crowdfunding-Plattform ist ein Indikator für Krisen.

nzz.title: «Mr. President, Ihre Massnahmen gegen die Migration gehen zu weit!» Republikaner fürchten einen Backlash der Latinos in den Zwischenwahlen
nzz.description: Wähler lateinamerikanischer Herkunft wenden sich von der Regierungspartei ab. Die bedrängte republikanische Abgeordnete Salazar greift Trump für seine aggressive Migrationspolitik an.

nzz.title: Die Wahlen im Nordosten Deutschlands sind auch ein Votum über Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz
nzz.description: In Berlin und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern dürfte die AfD ihre Wähleranteile erneut deutlich steigern, auch wenn die Partei keine Regierungsbeteiligung erhält. Für CDU und SPD steht viel auf dem Spiel.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Ursula von der Leyens Schwäche: Sie erfindet ständig Neues, statt Bestehendes durchzusetzen
nzz.description: Diese Woche hat die EU-Kommissions-Präsidentin ein komplexes Gesetz zu sozialen Netzwerken vorgestellt. Zudem möchte sie Kanada als «assoziiertes Mitglied» in die EU aufnehmen. Wer ständig so visionär denkt, scheitert fast zwangsläufig.

nzz.title: Baut Iran sein Atomprogramm wieder auf? Neue Satellitenbilder zeigen verdächtige Aktivitäten
nzz.description: Teheran renoviert eine Militäranlage, die im Zusammenhang mit dem Nuklearprogramm steht und schon zweimal bombardiert wurde. Ob die Iraner Atomwaffen derzeit wirklich herstellen können, ist aber fraglich. Nun droht Donald Trump erneut mit Angriffen.

nzz.title: Trotz Sanktionen schickt Nordkorea Arbeiter ins Ausland – und verdient so bis zu 800 Millionen Dollar
nzz.description: Vor allem in Russland nimmt die Zahl nordkoreanischer Arbeiter stark zu. Deren Einkommen geht zum grössten Teil an das Kim-Regime.

observador.title: Luís Montenegro. "Não vou ser o pai da austeridade"
observador.description: Primeiro-ministro recusa "ilusão" de apoios que contrariem subida dos combustíveis. E recusa medidas "facilitistas" que no passado pressionaram as contas públicas. "Não vou ser o pai da austeridade".

observador.title: Dívida pública francesa subirá para recorde en 2027
observador.description: O nível de endividamento de França vai continuar a aumentar, atingindo 119,3% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) em 2026 e 121,7% em 2027, níveis recorde.

observador.title: 13h. PM reforça importância do equilíbrio de contas públicas
observador.description: Luís Montenegro diz que "não quer ser o pai da austeridade". Ainda, a compra de 13,7 porcento do capital da REN custou ao estado 100 mil euros em assessoria.

observador.title: Gronelândia."Quem garante a dissuasão no Ártico são os EUA"
observador.description: A especialista em relações internacionais, Liliana Reis, diz que o acordo entre Dinamarca e EUA prova que a segurança é definida por "quem tem capacidade" e alerta que a UE "não tem força suficiente".

observador.title: Passos exige um Montenegro "à altura da tradição do PSD"
observador.description: Antigo primeiro-ministro reitera que gostava que o Governo "ousasse mais" no sentido de avançar com reformas. Responde a Leonor Beleza e afasta possibilidade de promover outro partido: "Sou do PSD".

observador.title: IL pede esforço ao Estado para que portugueses vivam melhor
observador.description: Líder da Iniciativa Liberal, Mariana Leitão, exigiu esforço ao Estado para que portugueses vivam melhor e defendeu proposta do partido que permitiria pagar menos 30 cêntimos por litro de combustível.

observador.title: Aluno de Almada já tem escola, após condenação do Ministério
observador.description: O aluno do concelho de Almada com necessidades educativas especiais, que o Ministério da Educação foi condenado a colocar naquele município, "já se encontra colocado na Escola Básica das Lagoas".

observador.title: Festas da Moita. Detidos mais de 50 condutores por álcool
observador.description: A GNR deteve na madrugada de hoje mais de 50 condutores por excesso de álcool em quatro horas de operação especial de fiscalização rodoviária no âmbito das Festas da Moita.

observador.title: Irão acusa organizadores de maratona de mulheres sem véu
observador.description: O Ministério Público de Teerão apresenta acusações contra os organizadores de uma maratona pela participação de mulheres sem o véu islâmico, cujas imagens se tornaram virais nas redes sociais.

observador.title: "OE 2027. "Não deve desvalorizar o investimento privado"
observador.description: O presidente da CPI, Armindo Monteiro, defende a aposta no investimento no próximo Orçamento de Estado. Já Tiago Oliveira da CGTP critica a política do Governo assente em baixos salários.

observador.title: Rui Borges fala muito porque não tem as costas quentes?
observador.description: Já se percebeu que os adeptos não morrem de amores por Rui Borges, mas as justificações acalmam os ânimos? Arouca tenta surpreender em Alvalade. Clássico vai realmente agitar as contas do campeonato?

observador.title: Pontualidade dos comboios abaixo do nível recomendado
observador.description: Infraestruturas de Portugal aponta as obras de modernização em curso em várias linhas para explicar a degradação dos níveis de pontualidade para 70%. Atrasos são maiores nos serviços de longo curso.

observador.title: 12h. OE 2027. CIP defende aposta no investimento privado
observador.description: Proposta do Orçamento de Estado vai ser apresentada até ao dia 10 do próximo mês e ainda não tem aprovação garantida. Ainda, Dinamarca confirma acordo com Estados Unidos sobre Gronelândia.

observador.title: A "Noruega alternativa" da princesa Martha Louise e do xamã
observador.description: Uma semana após o funeral de Harald V, Martha Louise estreou "Alternative Norge", série com os bastidores de sessões de vidência, bruxas e comunicação com animais.

observador.title: Estado pagou 100 mil euros a assessores da compra da REN
observador.description: A aquisição de 13,7% do capital da REN ao empresário espanhol pelo Estado envolveu a contratação de assessoria jurídica e financeira da Sérvulo Asssociados e da Caixa BI por 100 mil euros.

observador.title: Luís Montenegro quer imitar Sócrates e assustar Carneiro?
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro lançou um pacote de 800 milhões sem perguntas da imprensa, enquanto Carneiro deu um tiro no pé com o IVA. E ainda, as sondagens castigam a AD e o Moedas culpa o Volta pelo lixo.

observador.title: 11h. Portugal obrigado a executar programa Volta
observador.description: Normas europeias não permite recuar no sistema de recolha. Ainda neste jornal, continuam esta manhã as operações de rescaldo após o incêndio esta madrugada no Porto.

observador.title: Montenegro ativa o sino que fecha a bolsa de Nova Iorque
observador.description: Luís Montenegro vai participar pela segunda vez na Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, em Nova Iorque, na próxima semana. E vai acionar o sino que marca o fecho da bolsa de Nova Iorque.

spiegel.title: Désirée Nosbusch: Armbruch beim Eislaufen (im Sommer) während Filmvorbereitungen
spiegel.description: Sie habe sich nur auf einen Film vorbereiten wollen, sagt Désirée Nosbusch fast pflichtbewusst. Und dann kam ihr auf dem Eis eine andere Frau entgegen.

spiegel.title: F-35: Wichtige Flugzeugteile offenbar per Post nach Hongkong umgeleitet
spiegel.description: Gerade erst hat Deutschland die erste F-35 von den USA gekauft. Nun wird bekannt: Wichtige Teile eines solchen Kampfjets sind auf dem Weg in die Reparatur nach Hongkong umgeleitet worden. Dort verliert sich ihre Spur.

spiegel.title: Porsche: Personalabbau könnte drastischer ausfallen – weitere 4000 Jobs bedroht
spiegel.description: Der Personalabbau bei Porsche könnte drastischer ausfallen als bekannt. Laut einem Zeitungsbericht steht in einer Aufsichtsratsvorlage für den Mutterkonzern VW die Streichung von weiteren 4000 Jobs.

spiegel.title: Nordkorea: Unterirdische Atomtests lösen noch Jahre später Erdbeben aus
spiegel.description: Um ein nordkoreanisches Testgelände für Nuklearwaffen bebte fast 1400-mal die Erde, zeigt eine Studie. Die Erschütterungen nahmen nach dem Ende der Tests nicht wie erwartet ab, sondern zu.

spiegel.title: Sandro Mazzola ist tot: Der Maestro – Nachruf auf eine Inter-Legende
spiegel.description: Mailand trauert um Sandro Mazzola, einen der größten Fußballer Italiens. Er war der Anführer des großen Inter-Teams. Als Nationalspieler erlebte er aber auch bittere Enttäuschungen.

spiegel.title: Helga-Maria Schmid: Die Top-Diplomatin über die Kunst des Verhandelns
spiegel.description: Die Welt scheint aus den Fugen geraten. Hier erklärt Helga-Maria Schmid, wie Diplomaten vernünftig miteinander verhandeln können und warum Frauen unbedingt mit am Tisch sitzen sollten. Außerdem hat sie einen Tipp für private Verhandlungen.

spiegel.title: Berlin-Kreuzberg: Ein Mensch stirbt bei Feuer in Pflegeeinrichtung in Berlin
spiegel.description: Ein Zimmer einer Berliner Pflegeeinrichtung stand am Morgen in Vollbrand. Rettungs- und Pflegekräfte evakuierten das Haus, einer Person konnten sie nicht mehr helfen.

spiegel.title: AfD in Berlin: Was frustrierte Wähler im Osten der Stadt umtreibt
spiegel.description: Berlin gilt als weltoffen, tolerant, links. Bei der Abgeordnetenhauswahl wird die AfD aber vermutlich ein Rekordergebnis einfahren. Warum? Ein Ortstermin im Osten der Stadt.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: 340 Drohnen-Vorfälle über Militärstützpunkten in zwölf Monaten
spiegel.description: Die Drohnensichtungen über britischen Militärstützpunkten haben sich laut Bericht seit 2024 fast verdreifacht. Nun sollen zusätzliche Luftraumbeschränkungen verhängt werden.

spiegel.title: Oktoberfest: Warum die Frauenfiguren am Teufelsrad jetzt Radlerhosen tragen
spiegel.description: Den Frauenfiguren über dem »Teufelsrad« auf dem Oktoberfest wurden Radlerhosen unter den Rock gemalt. Gut so! Wer das prüde findet, hat vermutlich noch nie von »Upskirting« gehört.

spiegel.title: FC Bayern München: Sieben besondere Tore die zeigen, was diese Bayern ausmacht
spiegel.description: Der FC Bayern hat den höchsten Sieg der Saison gefeiert. Die Treffer gegen Union waren teils wunderschön und zeigen: Eigentlich sind die Münchner gar nicht zu verteidigen.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Flughafen München: Auto einer Reinigungsfirma stößt mit Flugzeug zusammen
spiegel.description: Zwischen Mitternacht und fünf Uhr gibt es keinen Flugverkehr am Münchner Airport. In dieser Nachtruhe hat es jetzt einen ungewöhnlichen Unfall gegeben.

spiegel.title: Ballon d’Or: Harry Kane will sich nach Aussagen von Lamine Yamal nicht am »Wahlkampf« beteiligen

phys-org.title: Florida scrub-jays attempt to breed at unusually young age after large-scale translocation
phys-org.description: For nearly two decades, biologist Lauren Deaner has worked with Florida scrub-jays, contributing to population recovery efforts and translocations. Now, as a doctoral researcher in UCF's integrative biology program, she is using that field experience to investigate how genetics, behavior and population dynamics influence the long-term recovery of imperiled species.

phys-org.description: Scientists map the hidden protein network that helps red blood cells adapt to oxygen

phys-org.title: Loss of Y chromosome in men could be an early warning sign of cancer
phys-org.description: A study initiated by Dr. Dan Theodorescu, a physician-scientist at the University of Arizona Cancer Center, revealed that the loss of the Y chromosome in men's body tissue could pave the way for cancer to develop. According to research recently published in JCI Insights, the loss of the chromosome, which is common in men as they age, creates a preneoplastic field effect, a hidden zone of genetic vulnerability in normal tissue that provides fertile ground for cancer to develop.

phys-org.title: Scientists simulate cosmic crashes to test whether icy moons gain or lose their ability to sustain life
phys-org.description: Many of the moons orbiting Saturn, Uranus and Neptune likely conceal oceans of liquid water beneath miles of icy shell. Because life as we know it needs water, these buried oceans rank among the most promising places to search for life beyond Earth.

phys-org.title: Kids involved with child protective services miss much more school than their peers
phys-org.description: Across the country, kids are settling into new school-year routines. Parents buy backpacks, teachers arrange desks and lesson plans, and friends reconnect. But in recent years, empty chairs are becoming a more common sight—especially in classrooms where students are already facing the most adversity.

phys-org.title: Sea surface temperature biases shift the North Pacific jet stream southward, study finds
phys-org.description: Climate models are numerical models used to project future climate change. They simulate the climate from the present into the future by calculating changes in the atmosphere, ocean and other components of the climate system. However, simulations of the present-day climate do not perfectly reproduce observations and contain various biases. The model characteristics that cause these biases can also affect simulations of the future climate. Understanding the causes and impacts of present-day clima

phys-org.title: Improving urban flood forecasting with real-time hazardous rainfall detection
phys-org.description: The Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology (KICT) announced that it will apply its early detection technology for quasi-stationary linear rainbands and sudden localized torrential rainfall to the Urban Flood Forecasting Platform operated by the Han River Flood Control Office in Korea for urban flood forecasting.

phys-org.title: How rural policing gaps can make escaping domestic violence harder
phys-org.description: Before murdering Molly Ticehurst in April 2024, court documents show Daniel Billings had threatened to exploit the limits of policing in her country town: "I will come in the middle of the night … The police won't stop me. I will get to you quicker than they will."

phys-org.title: Peer sexual harassment emerges early, highlighting need for prevention before Grade 4
phys-org.description: Sexual harassment between peers begins as early as Grade 4 and continues throughout lower secondary school. Most of those who sexually harass others have also experienced harassment themselves. These are among the findings of a doctoral thesis in psychology by Aziz-Kaan Dönmez from the University of Gothenburg, who studied peer sexual harassment among Swedish children and adolescents in Grades 4–9. Dönmez will defend his thesis on October 2.

phys-org.title: Scientists hope deeper-rooted soybeans can withstand climate extremes and store more carbon
phys-org.description: Research scientist Ashish Rajurkar kneels in the dirt, lifting a large clod of soil tangled around a soybean plant. He knocks away pieces of earth from the plant's roots, which slope straight down instead of out to the side like typical soybean plants.

phys-org.title: North Korea's nuclear testing may have triggered hundreds of earthquakes over several years
phys-org.description: Between 2006 and 2017, North Korea conducted six underground nuclear tests at its vast testing site at Mount Mantap in North Hamgyong province. Typically, underground explosions trigger an intense burst of minor earthquakes that die down once testing stops. But geologists have detected far more seismic activity after the final detonation, and it has persisted for years.

phys-org.title: Medieval Chinese skeleton may reveal first evidence of a brutal punishment
phys-org.description: Ancient Chinese authorities used many creative ways to punish people, often with methods designed to mark them for life. One brutal example mentioned repeatedly in historical texts is cutting off a person's nose. However, archaeologists in China have never found skeletal evidence to prove that it occurred. But that may have changed following the discovery of a skeleton of a woman who lived in China about 700 years ago.

phys-org.title: Workplace AI adoption remains slow, informal and uneven, survey finds
phys-org.description: Despite the rapid development of generative AI and the high level of public interest, the use of AI in the day-to-day work of many employees is not yet the norm. This is the finding of the third wave of the Konstanz AI study, for which a total of 1,105 employees were surveyed in May 2026. The proportion of employees who use AI in their work rose only slightly from 35% to 38% compared with the previous year.

phys-org.title: To read 2,000-year-old burned scrolls, scientists burn their own
phys-org.description: Douglas Seiler painstakingly sourced papyrus and reed pens from Egypt and traditional lampblack ink from Japan, then paid some high school students to inscribe the papyrus with lines from Star Wars and the Bible and a quote from the '60s sci-fi TV show The Outer Limits.

phys-org.title: Power breeds suspicion: In cases of wrongdoing, people point to leaders more quickly
phys-org.description: People with power are more quickly singled out as the culprit when something goes wrong but it is unclear who made the mistake. That is shown by a series of studies by researchers at the University of Amsterdam. In one, they analyzed almost 100,000 everyday conflicts on the Reddit page "Am I the Asshole?" According to the researchers, people with power are more readily blamed because others think they can "get away with anything." The findings are published in the Journal of Personality and Soci

phys-org.title: Europe can lower emissions without deindustrializing, say researchers
phys-org.description: The European Union has committed to achieving climate neutrality by 2050, a process that will require rapid and substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions across all economic sectors.

phys-org.title: Amino acids and a bone mineral may help control magnesium implant breakdown, three student papers suggest
phys-org.description: Seeing a bachelor's thesis published in a scientific journal is relatively uncommon. For three theses linked to the same research group to result in scientific publications within just three months is downright rare. Yet that is exactly what has happened in Elsebeth Schröder's research group at the Division of Quantum Device Physics.

phys-org.title: Physicists extend the search for quantum black holes at the LHC
phys-org.description: Physicists at UC Santa Barbara have extended the search for evidence of microscopic black holes produced at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). The formation of these tiny, fleeting objects at the LHC represents one way theorists have sought to resolve anomalies in our understanding of the basic structure of spacetime, while the method used to look for them demonstrates a new way of searching for new particles.

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s AI Opportunity
proj-syn.description: The global AI revolution is often portrayed as a Sino-American race to develop the most advanced frontier models. But the greatest economic prize most likely will be found in deploying practical intelligence, particularly in Africa’s young, dynamic, and fast-growing economies.

proj-syn.title: The Political Earthquake From Germany’s China Shock
proj-syn.description: For decades, Germany’s stability rested on an implicit bargain: high-value manufacturing would provide good jobs, strong export revenues, and broad-based prosperity, which political institutions would translate into social cohesion. Competition from China shakes that bargain to its foundations.

proj-syn.title: Stopping the Far Right’s Rise
proj-syn.description: Leftists insist that what is behind the far right’s recent gains, from Europe to Central and South America, is economic precarity. Far-right leaders know better, winning elections or gaining support despite embracing very different economic policies.

proj-syn.title: Does Claude Have Rights?
proj-syn.description: Given the many differences between brains and LLMs, claiming that an AI is or might be conscious requires a high bar of evidence. But Anthropic’s constitution for Claude brushes that caveat aside, suggesting that we attribute sentience to non-biological beings.

proj-syn.title: A Congress for Europe’s Future
proj-syn.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's recently proposed Congress of Europe is a step in the right direction, given the scale of Europe's geopolitical challenges. But to succeed, it must address the shortcomings that have hampered similar efforts in the past.

proj-syn.title: Can Adaptation Accelerate Climate Action?
proj-syn.description: After a summer of apocalyptic headlines, a new survey finds that people across the political spectrum are deeply concerned about preparing for the effects of global warming. The adaptation imperative may end up being the kind of crisis that forces us to stop neglecting the green agenda and act at the necessary scale.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Iran Sanctions Have a China Problem
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump is trying to pressure the Iranian regime by isolating it from the dollar-based financial system. But because Iran’s oil trade largely moves through Chinese banks and renminbi-based networks, those sanctions increasingly depend on financial institutions beyond American control.

proj-syn.title: When AI Stops Asking Permission
proj-syn.description: The most useful lesson from this summer’s breach of Hugging Face by a swarm of OpenAI agents is about architecture, not intentions. AI agents need protective layers—limited access, separate authorization for sensitive actions, records nobody can quietly edit, and outside testing before deployment—not a lecture about good behavior.

proj-syn.title: Are Mexicans Really Better Off Under Claudia Sheinbaum?
proj-syn.description: For two consecutive years, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has pointed to reductions in extreme poverty to argue that Mexicans are better off today than they were in 2018. But a more holistic look at the available socioeconomic data casts doubt on that rosy picture.

proj-syn.title: The UN’s Credibility Test
proj-syn.description: Effective multilateralism depends on institutions that are transparent, accountable, and able to enforce their own rules. The United Nations should lead by example, from how it selects its next secretary-general to how it plans to ensure that governments follow through on their climate commitments.

proj-syn.title: A Workable Social Contract for the Climate Transition
proj-syn.description: Economic insecurity and growing distrust in institutions are undermining governments’ ability to sustain support for climate action. To rebuild that support, they must show that climate policies can reduce household bills, create decent jobs, and ensure that the biggest emitters pay their fair share.

proj-syn.title: It’s Time to Reconsider Inflation Targeting
proj-syn.description: Central banks were caught off guard by the inflationary surge of 2021–23 because they relied too heavily on inflation forecasts based on flawed models and ignored other warning signs. Their failure to recognize the rapid growth of the money supply, in particular, underscores the need to reassess their reliance on inflation targeting.

proj-syn.title: Democrats Need to Talk About Immigration
proj-syn.description: Radical right-wing parties have advanced across Western countries by successfully tying immigration to voters’ diffuse fears about their economic well-being, personal security, and cultural identity. Rather than ignoring or co-opting such claims, mainstream parties must offer equally robust counternarratives.

proj-syn.title: War in an Age of Weak Powers
proj-syn.description: The war in Iran has weakened both the United States and China, exposing the limits of their military power and strategic influence. Their troubles are creating a more dangerous geopolitical landscape while providing Europe with a rare opportunity to reform its governance model and reinvent its global role.

proj-syn.title: Hedging the AI Doomsday Risk
proj-syn.description: As far-fetched as warnings of an impending AI apocalypse may sound, even a remote risk should not be dismissed outright when human extinction is at stake. To guard against a danger of such extraordinary scale, governments and companies need to go beyond conventional risk-management strategies.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Only as Trustworthy as the Internet
proj-syn.description: Trust in technology is eroding at the very moment AI is putting more power in the hands of governments and Big Tech. Rebuilding that trust requires keeping the internet open and accessible so that new technologies can develop through broad participation rather than being shaped by the interests of a powerful few.

proj-syn.title: AI Demands Simpler Financial Regulation
proj-syn.description: AI could undermine financial oversight by giving market participants new ways to circumvent rules that regulators never anticipated. Overly complicated regulations give AI agents more ways to game the system, underscoring the need to streamline existing frameworks and equip officials with AI tools of their own.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Asset Europe Has Overlooked
proj-syn.description: Europe’s soil is gradually dying, and yet the continent has still not recognized it as a strategic asset. Fortunately, the EU has many of the tools it needs to act, but doing so will require an overarching framework that helps farmers access financial rewards for measurable soil outcomes.

crunchbase.title: What 25,000 Startup Applications Reveal About The New Rules Of Seed-Stage Startups
crunchbase.description: The most-fundable startups prioritize a clear go-to-market strategy and test distinctive marketing channels early, treating distribution and disciplined focus as durable competitive advantages, explains guest author Aaron Golbin, a co-founder and general partner at LvlUp Ventures, who believes that seed-stage success depends on focused execution, diversified financing, built-in distribution, rapid learning and AI designed as core infrastructure.
